audit_findings.title: The 2025 tax burden is neither cash-normalized nor durable
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 tax expense $18.0 million versus $113.0 million cash taxes, a $95.0 million gap equal to 22.2% of the $427.0 million anchor; Singapore tax-status benefit $26.1 million; durable adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor's tax deduction directly determines owner earnings, and any understated recurring tax burden is then compounded through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2017, this agreement was extended to 2027 in exchange for revised employment and spending commitments.
audit_findings.explanation: The unusually low reported tax expense, large deferred-tax benefit, cash-tax gap, and 2027 expiration of the Singapore arrangement are demonstrated. It is not yet demonstrated that the $427.0 million anchor actually deducted only book tax or that the full $95.0 million timing gap is recurring. Nevertheless, the identified gap is large relative to the anchor and reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor tax deduction to the current tax provision and cash taxes by jurisdiction, separate timing and discrete items, estimate the post-2027 recurring tax rate, and rerun every scenario with the normalized tax burden.

audit_findings.title: The anchor and forecast perimeter may mix a disposed business with one-time charges
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.9 million disposal loss plus $29.7 million restructuring charges, or $40.6 million gross identified charges equal to 9.5% of the anchor; disposed-business owner earnings unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing disposal and nonrecurring restructuring charges would increase anchor owner earnings, while removing pre-sale earnings of the disposed business would decrease it; the net perimeter adjustment flows through all forecast years and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fourth quarter of 2025, the Company completed the sale of its small, industrial specialty chemicals business that reports within the MS segment and was presented as Held for Sale as of December 31, 2024 and 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The sale and identified charges are demonstrated, but the record does not show how the $427.0 million anchor treated them or quantify the disposed business's 2025 owner earnings. The direction and net amount therefore remain unresolved, and materiality cannot be established from the gross charges alone.
audit_findings.action: Construct a post-disposal 2025 owner-earnings reconciliation, separately identify the disposed business's revenue, operating profit, taxes, working capital and maintenance capital, classify each restructuring component as recurring or nonrecurring, and rerun the scenarios using the resulting like-for-like anchor.

audit_findings.title: Future interest costs may not match the equity-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 hedge benefit $7.9 million; June 2026 debt $3.495 billion, including $400.0 million due in 2028, $2.200 billion due in 2029 and $895.0 million due in 2030; refinancing-rate effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level owner-earnings model, interest remains inside owner earnings; refinancing costs therefore reduce forecast owner earnings rather than entering through a separate debt deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Any refinancing of our debt could be at higher interest rates and may require us to comply with more onerous covenants, which could further restrict our business operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The hedge expiration and debt maturity schedule are demonstrated, but higher refinancing coupons are forward-looking rather than a presently demonstrated error. Debt repayment also reduced the term loan to $200.0 million by June 2026, so the net future interest path cannot be inferred solely from the expired hedge.
audit_findings.action: Maintain a maturity-by-maturity debt schedule incorporating scheduled and voluntary repayments, the expired swap, current fixed coupons and explicit refinancing-rate cases, then verify that each forecast year's owner earnings includes the corresponding after-tax interest expense.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $353.6 million bridge add-back, including $287.8 million of non-U.S. cash; filed remittance-tax estimate $26.1 million; removing the entire add-back reduces base value by $2.27 per share from $40.75 to $38.48
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for operations, restricted by jurisdiction or subject to remittance tax should be excluded from the nonoperating-asset bridge or added net of the associated cost.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, there were approximately $393.2 million of accumulated undistributed earnings of subsidiaries outside of the United States, all of which are considered to be indefinitely reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the cash is surplus and freely distributable is unresolved. However, the entire questioned add-back is bounded by $353.6 million, only 5.6% of base equity value. Even the extreme assumption of removing all cash leaves base value at $38.48 per share, still far below the $138.74 market price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain June 2026 cash by jurisdiction, legal restrictions, covenant and operating-liquidity requirements, and applicable remittance taxes; revise the bridge only if needed for precision.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement obligations may be an omitted senior economic claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $32.5 million at December 31, 2025, equal to $0.21 per share and 0.5% of $6.353 billion base equity value; June 2026 ARO balance unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If expected settlement cash is not already captured in maintenance capital expenditure or other owner-earnings deductions, the unfunded obligation is a claim on equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has asset retirement obligations (“AROs”) related to environmental disposal obligations associated with certain restoration obligations associated with certain of its leased facilities, and cylinders used to supply customers with gas products.
audit_findings.explanation: The year-end obligation is demonstrated, but double omission is not: maintenance capital or operating expenditures may already fund the settlements. Even treating the full filed balance as an additional bridge deduction changes base value by only about $0.21 per share, which is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 ARO roll-forward and expected settlement schedule, trace associated restoration and cylinder-replacement spending into maintenance capital expenditure, and deduct only any demonstrated unfunded amount.

audit_findings.title: The diluted-share ceiling combines award and share counts from different dates
audit_findings.magnitude: up to 3.2 million potentially duplicated shares, 2.1% of the 155.9 million denominator; eliminating the full 3.2 million raises base value from $40.75 to approximately $41.60 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Double-counted vested or exercised awards inflate fully diluted shares and reduce calculated value per share without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: As of February 6, 2026, 152.0 million shares of the registrant’s Common Stock were outstanding.
audit_findings.explanation: Using counts from different dates is demonstrated, but actual double counting is only a possibility until the awards are rolled forward. Even the maximum case in which all 3.2 million added awards are duplicated increases base value by only about $0.85 per share, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged relative to the $138.74 market price.
audit_findings.action: Roll December 2025 options, RSUs and performance awards through June 27, 2026, remove exercises, vesting, forfeitures and settlements already reflected in the 152.7 million outstanding shares, apply treasury-stock treatment where appropriate, and recompute per-share values.
